explanation: The 'which integers are u-invariants?' problem (Kaplansky 1953; Merkurjev–Parimala 2025 §5.1; Karpenko's 2026 preprint summarises what is known: 1, all 2-powers, all even numbers, 9, 2^r+1 and everything except 2^r−1, 2^r−3 are attained, and 3, 5, 7 are not). The formal statement characterises the set u_invariant_values.answer as exactly {n | IsUInvariant n}, where IsUInvariant n says some char ≠ 2 field (in Type, justified by Löwenheim–Skolem) has n as the greatest dimension of a nondegenerate anisotropic form, as checked in the variant audits. A set-valued 'determine the answer' statement; faithful.
